title: 医療版マクロ経済スライドは「調整弁」の争いに　主戦場は窓口負担か
extracted_text:
1月の衆院解散で中断していた自民党と日本維新の会の社会保障改革に向けた協議が3月から再び始まった。焦点の一つとなるのが、経済成長率や人口動態に応じて医療費の伸びに上限を設ける「医療版マクロ経済スライド」の導入だ。

両党が2025年10月に交わした連立合意書の社会保障分野は13項目ある。冒頭に掲げたのが「インフレ下での医療給付費のあり方と、現役世代の保険料負担抑制との整合性を図るための制度的対応」だ。

議論再開初日の3月19日はこの項目を話し合い、維新は医療費の伸びを名目GDP（国内総生産）に連動させる仕組みを提起した。

年金では04年の制度改正で、支給額を経済状況に応じて自動的に抑えるマクロ経済スライドが導入された。医療にも同じような総額管理を適用しようとする議論は、四半世紀前から繰り返されてきた。

代表例は小泉純一郎政権下の01年。厚生労働省は70歳以上を対象に当時の老人医療費制度へ伸び率の抑制目標を導入する案を打ち出した。財務省は医療費全体を対象とし、目標超過分は診療報酬引き下げで調整する対案を唱えた。ともに実現に至らなかった。

年金や介護も含めた社会保障費は野放しに膨らんできたわけではない。例えば16年度予算以降は、毎年の国費について高齢化の伸びの範囲に抑える歳出の目安が導入された。

財務省の幹部は「デフレ時代だった当時は経済・物価が動かない分、高齢化の範囲までは面倒を見ようという考えだった。インフレで人件費や物件費があがる時代の医療費の伸びを抑えようとするならマクロ経済スライド的な発想が必要になる」と話す。

布石は打たれている。片山さつき財務相と上野賢一郎厚生労働相は25年12月、閣僚折衝の合意文書に「27年度の社会保障負担率が25年度と比較して上昇しないよう取り組む」との一文を盛り込んだ。年金や介護も含めた負担率は国民所得比で25年度に17.8%を見込む。

医療は年金とは異なる。新型コロナウイルスのようなパンデミック（世界的な大流行）や高額な新薬の登場といったイノベーションを伴い、予測が難しい。厚労省幹部は医療費の伸びに枠をはめれば「産業としての医療を抑え込みかねない」と危惧する。

いまも高齢化の伸びをはみ出す分は制度改革でカットしている。その上で保険料の負担率を一定にコントロールするなら、伸び続ける医療費の「調整弁」は患者が受診時に払う窓口負担か、税財源を増やすしかない。

維新は現役世代の保険料負担抑制を掲げ、消費税については高市早苗首相と歩調を合わせ2年間に限り食料品の税率をゼロとする立場を取る。公費と保険料で賄う給付費を抑え込むのなら、窓口負担の引き上げが選択肢にならざるを得ない。

赤字国債の発行拡大に頼る余裕が財政にない以上、痛みの再分配が改革の成否を決める。両党は5月末までに骨子をつくり、年度内に具体的な制度設計に入る。

translated_text:
Negotiations between the Liberal Democratic Party and Japan Innovation Party for social security reform, interrupted by the Lower House dissolution in January, resumed in March. One key focus is the introduction of a "medical macroeconomic slide" - a system that caps medical expense growth in line with economic growth rates and demographic changes.

The social security section of the coalition agreement signed by both parties in October 2025 contains 13 items. At the top is "institutional measures to align medical benefit costs under inflation with suppressing premium burdens on the working generation."

On March 19, the first day of resumed discussions, they debated this item, with Innovation Party proposing a mechanism linking medical expense growth to nominal GDP.

In pensions, a macroeconomic slide system that automatically restrains benefit amounts based on economic conditions was introduced in the 2004 reform. Similar discussions about applying total expenditure management to healthcare have been recurring for a quarter century.

A prime example was under the KoizumiJunichiro administration in 2001. The Ministry of Health proposed introducing a growth rate cap target for medical expenses for those 70 and older under the then-elderly medical system. The Ministry of Finance countered with a proposal targeting overall medical expenses, adjusting excess amounts through reductions in medical service fees. Neither was realized.

Social security costs including pensions and nursing care haven't expanded unchecked. For example, since the FY2016 budget, annual national expenditure guidelines have been introduced to hold increases within the scope of aging-related growth.

A senior Finance Ministry official said, "During the deflation era, since the economy and prices weren't moving, there was a mindset of covering up to the extent of aging. If we try to restrain medical expense growth in an era of inflation where personnel and material costs are rising, a macroeconomic slide-type approach becomes necessary."

Groundwork has been laid. Finance Minister Katayama Satsuki and Health Minister Ueno Kenichiro included a phrase in their December 2025 cabinet-level negotiation agreement document stating they "will work to ensure the social security burden rate for FY2027 does not increase compared to FY2025." The burden rate including pensions and nursing care is projected at 17.8% of national income for FY2025.

Healthcare differs from pensions. It's difficult to predict due to innovations like pandemics such as COVID-19 and expensive new drugs. Health Ministry officials fear that imposing limits on medical expense growth could "stifle healthcare as an industry."

Even now, portions exceeding aging-related growth are being cut through structural reforms. On top of that, if premium burden rates are to be kept constant, the only "adjustment valves" for continuously rising medical expenses are patient out-of-pocket costs at medical institutions or increasing tax funding.

Innovation Party advocates suppressing premium burdens on the working generation, and on consumption tax, aligns with Prime Minister Ishiba's position of limiting the food tax rate to zero for two years. If containing benefit costs through public funds and premiums is the goal, raising out-of-pocket costs becomes an unavoidable option.

With no room to rely on expanding deficit bond issuance, redistribution of pain will determine reform success. Both parties will create an outline by the end of May and begin specific institutional design within the fiscal year.
title_en: 'Medical Macroeconomic Slide' Becomes Fight Over 'Adjustment Valve' - Main Battlefield May Be Out-of-Pocket Costs
